Two people were killed, while several others sustained injuries during a clash between suspected rival cult groups at a masquerade procession in the Okepopo area of Lagos Island, Lagos State. PUNCH Metro learnt that the incident occurred on Saturday. It was gathered that the violence erupted when suspected members of a cult group allegedly attacked a rival, said to be a member of another cult group. The attack, however, triggered an immediate reprisal, leading to the death of one of the alleged attackers. A resident, who spoke to PUNCH Metro on Sunday on condition of anonymity due to the nature of the incident, said it happened quickly and threw the community into confusion. “Everything happened within a short period. The procession was ongoing around Agarawu and Okepopo when the attack occurred. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. One of the attackers was eventually killed,” the resident said. Another source familiar with the incident told our correspondent on Sunday that at least three other persons sustained serious injuries during the violence. The source noted that it was not the first time such an incident had occurred in the community. “At least three people were seriously injured during the fight. It started as a normal masquerade procession, with the participants moving from one street to another. LASG spends N120.8bn on ‘professional fees’ Lagos urged to unlock $2.5bn waste economy potential Detty December: Lagos warns visitors against hotel, ticket scams “Although this is not the first time such an incident has happened, there have been occasions when masquerade processions ended in fights in the community, as rival cult members sometimes use such gatherings to settle scores,” the source disclosed. The violence was also said to have forced residents and business owners to seek safety as the situation deteriorated. An anti-cultism advocacy platform, Naija Confra, which reported the incident in a post seen by PUNCH Metro on Sunday, also identified the deceased as Santana and Overbilling. According to the platform, the alleged attack on Santana was linked to the killing of an Aye member, identified as Jekomo, during another masquerade festival on October 17. It said the earlier incident occurred during the Egungun Ibi Deyin procession from Oje Alapini House, adding that Aye members accused Santana of being among those responsible for Jekomo’s death. The platform alleged that members of the Aye group secretly joined Saturday’s masquerade procession, during which Santana was present, and attacked him. It added that following Santana’s death, suspected Eiye members retaliated by killing Overbilling and attacking another alleged Aye member, who was reportedly rushed to a hospital. The platform, however, said the condition of the injured person remained unknown as of the time of its report. The state Police Public Relations Officer, Abimbola Adebisi, said she was not aware of the incident. She, however, promised to revert. She had yet to do so as of the time this report was filed.
